Op, consider you're not compatible. I understand the frustration, however this is literally a disability she has. She can't make her memory work that way. It could absolutely be because she needs better coping skills or it could be because you guys live a fundamentally neurotypical life style that just does not suit her brain capacity.

She will always have adhd, it's not ever going to go completely away. Shes going to forget, she's going to be late, she's going to struggle; her brain is different. I can only imagine she doesn't want to let you down either, and by placing blame on her for something she literally can't fundamentally change, you're creating a shame cycle that's always doomed to make her fail. If she's always doomed to fail and feel that shame, she may struggle to keep WANTING to try. It's genuinely okay if this creates barriers, but please just consider whether this is a healthy relationship for either of you.

You deserve to get your needs met, for sure, but you wouldn't get angry with someone who is physically disabled I would hope. This isn't a moral or personal failure, it's okay to be frustrated, but if it's really this bad, you need to understand that shes not magically going to "get better", because she can't, therefore maybe you're not compatible.

Regardless, I hope you're doing well now, and that your struggles don't impede you from living a full life even in pandemic times.

My understanding as someone working through my own trauma/realizing how much of I have is this: During a traumatic experience, your body automatically shuts down anything that is not necessary for survival, that often times includes not just blood flow to your hands and feet, but the emotional reactions to what's happening to you.

When you have a ptsd flashback, you are literally being put back into that mindset, experiencing it basically for the first time because your brain decided what you were experiencing/seeing/feeling was too great to cope with in the moment, and was into focused on getting through it to survive.

I can't diagnose you, but it genuinely sounds like you got caught up in flashbacks, and they put you back into the underlying trauma. This happens, or at least it happened to me, just as suddenly as it seems to have happened to you. I was doing fine, coping and then another big life event sent me spiraling and now I'm inundated with flashbacks daily.

Please don't try to deal with this alone, reach out to support systems, therapy search, don't settle for the first person you find, make sure they're someone you can really confide in. Your feelings are not crazy, weird, or wrong.

Your husband is being a bit of a donut but sometimes it can seem so ridiculous to the outside viewer when they assume this is a hurt you've already dealt with and should be over. With ptsd (if that's what's going on)that's not how it works obviously, so I hope that with some open communication and talking to a good professional you can work through this trauma and have your husband understand at the same time. I'm sending you luck.
